question.text: Reverse cash-and-carry arbitrage is suitable for those who:

answer.text: Already hold the commodity — they sell it in spot, invest the released funds, and buy futures when futures are underpriced relative to spot plus cost of carry
Want to buy physical commodity for immediate use
Have no access to the futures market
Want to speculate on rising commodity prices

explanation.text: The Logic: Reverse cash-and-carry is designed for those with asset holdings. The trade is initiated by selling the commodity in spot, lending/investing the released funds, and buying futures when the futures price is below spot plus cost of carry. The Trap: It is for current holders, not new buyers. It requires futures market access. It is arbitrage, not speculation. Note: The setup is not limited to backwardation; in the source example futures sit above spot but below the fair value implied by spot plus interest/carry cost.
